name: Diltiazem
route_note: oral immediate- and extended-release; IV for rapid rate control; compounded topical gel for anal fissure

discovery.note: A benzothiazepine developed in Japan in the late 1960s–70s and first marketed there as Herbesser.

tagline: Rate-slowing calcium channel blocker for angina and atrial fibrillation
summary: Diltiazem is a benzothiazepine calcium channel blocker that acts on both heart and blood vessels. It is used for angina, hypertension and, intravenously, for rapid control of ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation or flutter.
mechanism: Diltiazem blocks L-type calcium channels in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle. In the heart it slows sinoatrial node firing and atrioventricular conduction and modestly reduces contractility.
In vessels it dilates coronary and peripheral arteries. Its effects are intermediate between those of verapamil (more cardiac) and dihydropyridines (more vascular).
uses: Atrial fibrillation or flutter rate control (IV)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Cardizem for angina, marketed by Marion Laboratories.

history.title: MDPIT
history.detail: Diltiazem after MI shows no overall mortality benefit and harm in patients with pulmonary congestion.

history.title: Once-daily form
history.detail: Extended-release diltiazem (Cardizem CD) is approved in the US, allowing once-daily dosing for hypertension and angina.

history.title: NORDIL
history.detail: Diltiazem-based therapy is as effective as diuretics and beta-blockers in hypertension.

history.title: AF rate control guidance
history.detail: Guidelines of the 2010s list IV and oral non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers such as diltiazem as first-line rate-control options in atrial fibrillation without reduced ejection fraction.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4; active desacetyl metabolite; moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor

serious: Worsening heart failure with reduced EF

facts: It inhibits CYP3A4, raising levels of drugs such as simvastatin and ciclosporin.
